Install Pi with:

pi.startupTimeoutBusy:
Pi started but did not become ready within {{seconds}}s.

Pi was alive and producing output, but never answered the readiness check. Extension startup hooks run before Pi reads commands, and a hook that calls a local model server can wait this long while the model loads or prefills a large prompt. Check the engine and model-server logs, then retry.
pi.startupTimeoutSilentNoOutput:
Pi produced no output within {{seconds}}s.

No output captured. Check the app log for the exact spawn command, and try running `pi --mode rpc` directly in a terminal.

confirm.changeFolderMessage: Pi has not finished responding in this session. Changing the project folder restarts Pi, which stops it: whatever Pi already wrote to the session is kept, but the rest of the response — including any tool calls still running — is discarded.
confirm.cloneMessage: Pi has not finished responding in this session. Cloning this branch stops it: whatever Pi already wrote to the session is kept, but the rest of the response — including any tool calls still running — is discarded.
confirm.closeManagedWorktreeMessage: Close "{{name}}"? Clean worktrees are removed; tabs with uncommitted changes are preserved on disk.
confirm.closeSessionTabMessage: Pi is still working in this session. Closing the tab stops its runtime; saved messages remain available from Sessions.
confirm.closeUnmanagedWorktreeMessage: Close "{{name}}"? This existing worktree and its files remain on disk.
confirm.forkMessage: Pi has not finished responding in this session. Forking this session stops it: whatever Pi already wrote to the session is kept, but the rest of the response — including any tool calls still running — is discarded.
confirm.newMessage: Pi has not finished responding in this session. Starting a new session stops it: whatever Pi already wrote to the session is kept, but the rest of the response — including any tool calls still running — is discarded.
confirm.removeWorkspaceMessage: Remove "{{name}}" from the sidebar? Its Pi process stops; files on disk are not touched.
confirm.switchMessage: Pi has not finished responding in this session. Opening another session stops it: whatever Pi already wrote to the session is kept, but the rest of the response — including any tool calls still running — is discarded.
confirm.trustWorkspaceMessage: This workspace defines permission rules (.pi-desktop/permission-rules.json) with allow rules that would let Pi skip confirmation prompts. They are ignored until you trust this workspace; its deny rules always apply. Only trust workspaces from a source you trust.
confirm.workspaceMessage: Pi has not finished responding in this session. It keeps working after you switch: the response is saved to the session and restored when you come back, and any prompt Pi raises while you are away is held and shown on your return.
confirm.workspaceRulesNoticeMessage: This workspace defines its own permission rules (.pi-desktop/permission-rules.json). Its deny rules restrict Pi while you work here; your global rules apply otherwise.
